subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Packaging: From Die to Device
description: A short lesson to help you apply Packaging: From Die to Device.

hook.text: A silicon die is smaller than a fingernail. It needs a package to connect to the outside world.

buildup.text: Bond wires or solder bumps connect die pads to package pins. Heat spreaders manage thermal load.

discovery.text: Ball Grid Array (BGA) packages put solder balls underneath — hundreds of connections in a tiny space.

twist.text: Advanced packaging stacks dies vertically — 3D packaging. More function in less board space.

climax.text: Apple's M-series chips use system-in-package design: CPU, GPU, and memory in one module.

punchline.text: The package is the bridge between a microscopic die and the macroscopic world.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of chip packaging?
options: To add more transistors to the chip
To connect the silicon die to external circuits and manage heat
To protect the chip from electromagnetic interference only
